newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief condemns Rwanda killings.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief condemns Rwanda killings.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan condemned on Monday the killing in Rwanda of three Spanish aid workers and the wounding of an American, saying the violence underscored the need to find a solution to the problems of the Central African Great Lakes region.
A statement issued through U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said Annan was shocked by Sunday's attack on employees of Medecins du Monde (Doctors of the World) in Ruhengeri, northwestern Rwanda.

It said he "strongly condemns this act of violence against people whose efforts were to alleviate suffering and protect the vulnerable" and it offered Annan's deepest condolences to Medecins du Monde and to the families and governments of the victims of the "heinous attack."

"Continued instability and violence in the Great Lakes region underscore the importance of finding a lasting solution to the region's problems. He urges all parties to work together to this end and to ensure the safety and protection of relief workers," Eckhard added.
Reports from the area said Rwandan Hutu militiamen carried out the attack in which three Rwandan soldiers also died.
Eckhard said U.N. staff in Rwanda continued to work normally except those in the Ruhengeri region, who would do work only during daylight hours, returning to Kigali, the capital, in the evening.

He said the secretary-general expected to present the Security Council on Tuesday with proposals for dealing with the problems of the Great Lakes region, including the appointment of a joint special representative of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.
